The claim is false under those hypotheses: with $K=[0,1]$ and $f\equiv 2$, $f$ is continuous on a compact set but $\sup_K|f|=2>1$. The proof is explicitly omitted and no citation is given, so the assertion is left entirely unjustified; the later remark that the bound is "sharp for constant functions" only concerns sharpness and cannot establish it. To be supported, the section would need an added hypothesis (e.g. $\sup_K|f|\le 1$ by assumption, or $\|f\|_\infty$ normalized) or a proof/citation of the bound.
